WhatsApp basics

How much the WhatsApp Business API really costs in 2026 (worked out line by line)

The bill has three parts, and almost everyone gets the same one wrong. In our hypothetical example, a single line accounts for 85% of what goes to Meta.

LVBy Lucas Vaz·November 13, 2026·7 min read

Key takeaways

  • The WhatsApp API bill has three parts: the platform, Meta's fees per delivered message, and AI.
  • Messages customers send you are free. Since October 1, 2026, each number gets 1,000 free service replies per month.
  • In Brazil, a marketing message costs about 9 times a utility message on the rate card in effect since October 2026.
  • For a typical business, campaigns are the heaviest line on the Meta bill. Trimming the list is the fastest saving.
  • Run your own numbers in the calculator and always check Meta's official rates.

"How much does the WhatsApp Business API cost?" is the question I hear most from people moving off the free app. The honest answer starts with "it depends," which annoys every business owner I know. So let's do it differently: split the bill into parts, price each one, and work through a full example with numbers you can swap for your own.

Spoiler: for most businesses, the part that scares people isn't the part that costs money.

What are the parts of a WhatsApp API bill?

The API itself has no screen. You use it through a platform, and the final bill combines three different things, each charged by whoever provides it:

  1. The platform. A fixed monthly fee for the inbox, contacts, campaigns and a team sharing one number.
  2. Meta's fees. A price per delivered message, set by the message category and the recipient's country. It's usage, not a subscription.
  3. AI. If an assistant answers customers, someone pays for the processing. Some platforms bill it separately, in tokens, through your own OpenAI or Google account. Others include it in the plan.

Add your local taxes and you're done. If the difference between the free app and the API is still fuzzy, read the comparison of the WhatsApp Business app vs. the API first.

How much does Meta charge per message?

Since July 2025, Meta charges per delivered message instead of per conversation. Every message falls into a category, and the price depends on where your customer is. Here are the rates for Brazil, which we'll use in the example:

CategoryUsed forBrazil (US$)
MarketingOffers, news, invitations to come back0.0625
UtilityOrder confirmed, shipped, invoice, reminder0.0068
AuthenticationVerification codes0.0068
ServiceYour replies within 24 h of the customer's last message1,000 free/mo, then 0.0068

These come from Meta's rate card in effect since October 1, 2026, in USD per delivered message, before volume discounts. They're the same figures our calculator uses, and the calculator lets you pick other countries, where prices can be much lower or higher.

Three details change the math:

  • Meta can change rates on the first day of each quarter (January 1, April 1, July 1, October 1). Before you plan, check Meta's official WhatsApp Business pricing page.
  • Volume discounts exist, but only for utility and authentication. Marketing has no volume tiers.
  • Some countries are billed in local currency. Brazilian accounts, for example, are moving to billing in reais through Meta's local entity, with a published BRL rate card. If that applies to you, the local-currency rate is the one that counts.

What you're not charged for (and where most people get the math wrong)

The classic mistake is counting every message in the chat. People take the month's total messages, multiply by the marketing rate, and decide the API is way too expensive. The right math leaves several things out:

  • Everything the customer sends you. Always free, no matter how many photos and voice notes.
  • Your first 1,000 service replies each month, per WhatsApp number. Unused ones don't roll over.
  • Undelivered messages. An invalid number or a phone that never received it means no charge.
  • Customers who arrive from a Click-to-WhatsApp ad. If you reply within the 24-hour window, a free entry period opens during which messages aren't charged.

Another common mix-up is thinking there's a fee to "open a conversation." Not anymore. Each message has one category and is charged at most once. If the 24-hour rule still feels like a mystery, the guide to the WhatsApp 24-hour window explains it in three minutes.

How to calculate your WhatsApp API cost, step by step

Here's a hypothetical example: a women's clothing store with three salespeople answering from one number, selling to customers in Brazil. The numbers are made up to keep the math clean. Replace them with yours.

Step 1: service replies

The store hears from 600 customers a month on WhatsApp. On average, the team sends 5 replies per customer. That's 3,000 service messages.

The first 1,000 are free. The other 2,000 × US$0.0068 = US$13.60.

Step 2: utility notifications

There are 300 orders a month, and each gets two updates: order confirmed and order shipped. That's 600 utility messages × US$0.0068 = US$4.08.

Step 3: marketing campaigns

Two campaigns a month, each to 800 customers who agreed to receive offers. That's 1,600 messages × US$0.0625 = US$100.00.

Step 4: add it up

LineMessagesUS$
Service3,000 (1,000 free)13.60
Utility6004.08
Marketing1,600100.00
Meta total5,200117.68

Step 5: platform and AI

Now the subscription. With 600 customers handled by AI each month and campaigns to 1,600 contacts, this store would outgrow the Starter plan (500 AI conversations and 1,000 campaign contacts). On Kontaro it would be on Growth, US$129 a month, which includes 2,500 AI conversations and five team members. Paid yearly, with two months free, that's about US$108 a month.

Rough total: US$129 platform + US$117.68 Meta = about US$247 a month.

Look at the table again. Of 5,200 messages, the 1,600 marketing ones make up 85% of what the store pays Meta. Answering customers, the thing most people worry about, cost less than US$14.

Where the money actually goes: campaigns

At Brazil's rates, a marketing message costs about nine times a utility message. A thousand "your order is out for delivery" updates cost US$6.80. A thousand "weekend sale" messages cost US$62.50.

That has two practical consequences.

First, your send list is the biggest cost dial you have. If the store sent campaigns only to the 400 customers who bought in the last 90 days, the marketing line would drop from US$100 to US$50. It would probably sell almost as much, because people who haven't bought in two years rarely respond to a generic promotion.

Second, disguising marketing as utility doesn't work. Meta reviews template categories and moves them to marketing when it finds promotional content, even after approval. An order update with a coupon at the end becomes a marketing message. The guide on rejected WhatsApp templates shows how to write templates that land in the right category.

Where does AI fit in the bill?

Platforms vary a lot here, and this is where surprises show up. Token billing is hard to predict: a customer who sends ten long voice notes costs more than one who just asks your hours, and you find out at the end of the month.

The most predictable model is billing per conversation. That's how we do it: each customer the AI helps within 24 hours counts once, however many messages you exchange. If you hit the plan limit, the AI pauses and chats go to your team, with nothing charged automatically. If you want more, an extra pack is 1,000 conversations for US$25.

Whatever platform you pick, ask three questions before signing: Is AI included or billed separately? How is usage counted? What happens when the limit runs out?

How to pay less without serving customers worse

None of these steps mean answering less or replying slower:

Run your numbers before any sales call

Here's what I'd do today: open your business WhatsApp and count how many different customers talked to you in the last 30 days. Estimate how many replies each one got. Write down how many campaigns you send and to how many people.

With those three numbers, the Meta cost calculator gives you a monthly estimate in under a minute. It already subtracts the 1,000 free service replies for the month, assuming one WhatsApp number. If you use more than one number, each gets its own 1,000, so your real bill will land a bit below the estimate.

Walking into a vendor conversation already knowing those numbers means you negotiate better, choose the right plan, and don't get a shock from the first invoice.

Frequently asked questions

Does Meta charge a monthly fee for the WhatsApp API?

No. Meta doesn't charge for access. It charges per delivered message, based on the message category and the recipient's country. The monthly fee you pay belongs to the platform that gives you the inbox, AI and campaigns.

How much is a WhatsApp marketing message?

It depends on the recipient's country. For Brazil, Meta's rate card in effect since October 1, 2026 lists about US$0.0625 per delivered marketing message, before discounts. Meta can change rates on the first day of each quarter, so check the official page before planning a campaign.

Am I charged for messages that weren't delivered?

No. Meta only charges for delivered messages. If a number no longer exists or the message never reaches the phone, there's no fee for it.

Is replying to customers on WhatsApp free?

The first 1,000 service replies per number each month are free. From the 1,001st, Meta charges its official rate. Messages customers send you are never charged.
